classification.difficultyReason: Apply the equal-radius compass-arc construction to three different intervals.

content.prompt: Draw three different intervals and construct the perpendicular bisector of each interval.

answer.short: Three different intervals, each with a constructed line passing through its midpoint at right angles. Sample constructions are shown.
answer.worked: For each interval, draw arcs centred at its endpoints using the same radius, greater than half the interval's length. Keep this radius unchanged for the two endpoints. Draw the straight line through the two arc intersections. This line bisects the interval and is perpendicular to it. Repeat for two other intervals.

spec.description: Three authored sample intervals of different lengths and orientations, each with equal-radius intersecting compass arcs and its perpendicular bisector. Ordinary geometry and construction guides use black.
spec.mathematics: For an interval of length L, both endpoint arcs have radius 0.8L. Their intersections lie on the perpendicular line through the midpoint. Rotation preserves these relationships.
